title: Charting Cervical Spinal Cord Morphometry Across the Lifespan
authors: Kurt G. Schilling, Michael E. Kim, Matthew Amandola, Chenyu Gao, Karthik Ramadass, Praitayini Kanakaraj, Sam Bogdanov, Gaurav Rudravaram, Nancy R. Newlin, Derek Archer, Timothy J. Nguyen, Kathryn L. Humphreys, Yanbin Niu, Sophia Vinci-Booher, Carissa J. Cascio, The HABS-HD Study Team, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, The BIOCARD Study Team, Zhiyuan Li, Daniel Moyer, Simon N. summary: Reference charts describe cervical spinal cord size and shape from birth to age 100. The published models use 24,251 healthy or cognitively normal controls from 33 datasets. Cross-sectional area peaks around the mid-30s before declining.
description: The study screened 78,269 T1-weighted brain MRI sessions for cervical coverage and modeled six size and shape measures from C1 to C7. The charts provide age- and sex-specific centiles. The curves come from cross-sectional data and do not measure individual rates of change.
findings: The final reference cohort included 24,251 controls from 33 datasets.
Cross-sectional area peaks around the mid-30s.
The timing and magnitude of size and shape changes vary by cervical level.
